Parse a Smart Game Format game tree into nodes of properties and their child trees, with SGF's escaping rules for text values.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/sgf-parsing) (MIT). Listed under [Parsing & Validation](/examples/?subject=parsing-and-validation).

```nomi-run
// FILE: sgf_parsing.nomi
//# A parser for Smart Game Format (SGF) game trees whose values are all
//# SGF Text.

/// A node of the game tree: its properties, each key with one or more
/// values, and the trees that follow it.
pub struct Tree {
    properties: Map<String, List<String>>
    children: List<Tree>
}

/// Why the text is not a game tree.
pub enum Error {
    TreeMissing
    TreeWithNoNodes
    PropertiesWithoutDelimiter
    PropertyMustBeUppercase
    /// Anything else the grammar does not allow: an unclosed tree or value,
    /// or text after the tree.
    Malformed
}

/// The game tree `encoded` writes.
pub fn parse(encoded: String) -> Result<Tree, Error> {
    ['(', ..rest] = String.to_codepoints(encoded) else {
        return Err(.TreeMissing)
    }
    #(tree, rest) = try node(rest)
    if rest != [] { return Err(.Malformed) }
    Ok(tree)
}

/// A node from its `;` on, with what follows it: another node is its one
/// child, and parenthesized trees are its children. The node that ends a
/// sequence reads the `)` that closes the sequence's tree.
fn node(text: List<Codepoint>) -> Result<#(Tree, List<Codepoint>), Error> {
    [';', ..rest] = text else {
        return Err(.TreeWithNoNodes)
    }
    #(properties, rest) = try read_properties(rest, %{})

    #(children, rest) = case rest {
        [';', .._] -> {
            #(child, rest) = try node(rest)
            #([child], rest)
        }

        _ ->
            try variations(rest, [])
    }

    Ok(#(#Tree{properties, children}, rest))
}

/// The parenthesized trees after a node, up to and including the `)` that
/// closes the tree the node is in.
fn variations(
    text: List<Codepoint>,
    found: List<Tree>,
) -> Result<#(List<Tree>, List<Codepoint>), Error> {
    case text {
        ['(', ..rest] -> {
            #(tree, rest) = try node(rest)
            variations(rest, found + [tree])
        }

        [')', ..rest] ->
            Ok(#(found, rest))

        _ ->
            Err(.Malformed)
    }
}

/// A node's properties: each an upper-case key and one or more values.
fn read_properties(
    text: List<Codepoint>,
    found: Map<String, List<String>>,
) -> Result<#(Map<String, List<String>>, List<Codepoint>), Error> {
    key = text |> Iter.take_while(Codepoint.letter?) |> Iter.to_list()
    if key == [] { return Ok(#(found, text)) }

    if !Iter.all?(key, Codepoint.upper?) {
        return Err(.PropertyMustBeUppercase)
    }

    rest = text |> Iter.drop(Iter.count(key)) |> Iter.to_list()
    #(values, rest) = try read_values(rest, [])

    if values == [] {
        return Err(.PropertiesWithoutDelimiter)
    }

    read_properties(rest, Map.put(found, String.from_codepoints(key), values))
}

/// The bracketed values after a key.
fn read_values(
    text: List<Codepoint>,
    found: List<String>,
) -> Result<#(List<String>, List<Codepoint>), Error> {
    case text {
        ['[', ..rest] -> {
            #(value, rest) = try read_text(rest, "")
            read_values(rest, found + [value])
        }

        _ ->
            Ok(#(found, text))
    }
}

/// One value's text, up to its closing `]`. A `\` keeps the character
/// after it, except that a newline after it is removed; any whitespace
/// other than a newline becomes a space.
fn read_text(text: List<Codepoint>, value: String) -> Result<#(String, List<Codepoint>), Error> {
    case text {
        [']', ..rest] -> Ok(#(value, rest))
        ['\\', '\n', ..rest] -> read_text(rest, value)
        ['\\', c, ..rest] or [c, ..rest] -> read_text(rest, value + plain(c))
        [] or ['\\'] -> Err(.Malformed)
    }
}

fn plain(c: Codepoint) -> String {
    if c != '\n' and Codepoint.whitespace?(c) {
        " "
    } else {
        "${c}"
    }
}

// FILE: sgf_parsing_test.nomi
import sgf_parsing.{self, Error, Tree}

test "parse" {
    cases: List<#(String, String, Result<Tree, Error>)> = [
        #("empty input", "", Err(.TreeMissing)),
        #("tree with no nodes", "()", Err(.TreeWithNoNodes)),
        #("node without tree", ";", Err(.TreeMissing)),
        #("node without properties", "(;)", Ok(#{properties: %{}, children: []})),
        #("single node tree", "(;A[B])", Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["B"]},
                children: [],
            })),
        #(
            "multiple properties",
            "(;A[b]C[d])",
            Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["b"], "C" => ["d"]},
                children: [],
            }),
        ),
        #("properties without delimiter", "(;A)", Err(.PropertiesWithoutDelimiter)),
        #("all lowercase property", "(;a[b])", Err(.PropertyMustBeUppercase)),
        #("upper and lowercase property", "(;Aa[b])", Err(.PropertyMustBeUppercase)),
        #(
            "two nodes",
            "(;A[B];B[C])",
            Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["B"]},
                children: [
                    #{
                        properties: %{"B" => ["C"]},
                        children: [],
                    },
                ],
            }),
        ),
        #(
            "two child trees",
            "(;A[B](;B[C])(;C[D]))",
            Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["B"]},
                children: [
                    #{
                        properties: %{"B" => ["C"]},
                        children: [],
                    },
                    #{
                        properties: %{"C" => ["D"]},
                        children: [],
                    },
                ],
            }),
        ),
        #(
            "multiple property values",
            "(;A[b][c][d])",
            Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["b", "c", "d"]},
                children: [],
            }),
        ),
        #(
            "within property values, whitespace characters such as tab are converted to spaces",
            "(;A[hello\t\tworld])",
            Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["hello  world"]},
                children: [],
            }),
        ),
        #(
            "within property values, newlines remain as newlines",
            "(;A[hello\n\nworld])",
            Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["hello\n\nworld"]},
                children: [],
            }),
        ),
        #(
            "escaped closing bracket within property value becomes just a closing bracket",
            "(;A[\\]])",
            Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["]"]},
                children: [],
            }),
        ),
        #(
            "escaped backslash in property value becomes just a backslash",
            "(;A[\\\\])",
            Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["\\"]},
                children: [],
            }),
        ),
        #(
            "opening bracket within property value doesn't need to be escaped",
            "(;A[x[y\\]z][foo]B[bar];C[baz])",
            Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["x[y]z", "foo"], "B" => ["bar"]},
                children: [
                    #{
                        properties: %{"C" => ["baz"]},
                        children: [],
                    },
                ],
            }),
        ),
        #(
            "semicolon in property value doesn't need to be escaped",
            "(;A[a;b][foo]B[bar];C[baz])",
            Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["a;b", "foo"], "B" => ["bar"]},
                children: [
                    #{
                        properties: %{"C" => ["baz"]},
                        children: [],
                    },
                ],
            }),
        ),
        #(
            "parentheses in property value don't need to be escaped",
            "(;A[x(y)z][foo]B[bar];C[baz])",
            Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["x(y)z", "foo"], "B" => ["bar"]},
                children: [
                    #{
                        properties: %{"C" => ["baz"]},
                        children: [],
                    },
                ],
            }),
        ),
        #(
            "escaped tab in property value is converted to space",
            "(;A[hello\\\tworld])",
            Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["hello world"]},
                children: [],
            }),
        ),
        #(
            "escaped newline in property value is converted to nothing at all",
            "(;A[hello\\\nworld])",
            Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["helloworld"]},
                children: [],
            }),
        ),
        #(
            "escaped t and n in property value are just letters, not whitespace",
            "(;A[\\t = t and \\n = n])",
            Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["t = t and n = n"]},
                children: [],
            }),
        ),
        #(
            "mixing various kinds of whitespace and escaped characters in property value",
            "(;A[\\]b\nc\\\nd\t\te\\\\ \\\n\\]])",
            Ok(#{
                properties: %{"A" => ["]b\ncd  e\\ ]"]},
                children: [],
            }),
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, encoded, expected), description {
        assert sgf_parsing.parse(encoded) == expected
    }
}

// Not canonical cases: the canonical data has no case for text the grammar
// leaves unfinished or follows with more.
test "malformed trees" {
    cases = [
        #("a tree with no closing parenthesis", "(;A[B]"),
        #("a value with no closing bracket", "(;A[B)"),
        #("a value ending in a backslash", "(;A[B\\"),
        #("text after the tree", "(;A[B])x"),
        #("a child tree with no closing parenthesis", "(;A[B](;B[C])"),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, encoded), description {
        assert sgf_parsing.parse(encoded) == Err(Error.Malformed)
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- The parser is recursive descent over `String.to_codepoints`, one function per part of the grammar (`node`, `variations`, `read_properties`, `read_values`, `read_text`). Each answers what it read and the codepoints after it, `Result<#(T, List<Codepoint>), Error>`, and `try` passes a failure up. The delimiters are codepoint literals in list patterns, `[';', ..rest]` and `['\\', '\n', ..rest]` (style §19).
- A `;` after a node starts its one child, and `(` starts its variations. The node that ends a sequence reads the `)` that closes the sequence's tree, so `(;A[B];B[C])` needs no count of open parentheses.
- `Tree` is a struct of a `Map<String, List<String>>` and a `List<Tree>`, as the canonical data's JSON is shaped, so the expected trees in the tests are literals of it.
- SGF Text's rules are three arms of `read_text`: a `\` before a newline drops both, a `\` before anything else keeps that character, and any whitespace but a newline becomes a space. The escaped and unescaped character share one arm, `['\\', c, ..rest] or [c, ..rest]`.
- The canonical errors are variants of `Error`. Text the canonical data has no case for, an unclosed tree or value or text after the tree, is one more variant, `Malformed`; five tests marked as not canonical cover it.
- The canonical cases are one `subtests` table. The canonical data replaces "escaped property" with "mixing various kinds of whitespace and escaped characters in property value" (`reimplements`); the table holds only the replacement.
